# Column: sender_transaction_currency
Table: event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: Currency used in the transaction, e.g., USD, EUR, INR.
Sample Values: USD, INR, EUR
Related Business Terms: Currency, Transaction
Sample Usage:
  1. List transactions in INR currency
     `SELECT * FROM event_store WHERE sender_transaction_currency = 'INR'`

# Column: customer_email_last_update_at
Table: event_store
Data Type: INTEGER
Description: The last time the customer email was updated
Related Business Terms: email, customer, customer_email
Sample Usage:
  1. Get the last time the customer email was updated
     `SELECT customer_email_last_updated_at FROM event_store WHERE customer_id = 12345`

# Column: product_code
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: A unique identifier assigned to each product to facilitate tracking and identification within the company's inventory system. The code typically consists of alphanumeric characters.
Sample Values: PT001
Related Business Terms: Inventory Management, Product Identification, SKU

# Column: bulk_id
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: A unique identifier assigned to a group of transactions processed as a single batch. This identifier is used to track and manage bulk operations, ensuring accurate reporting and reconciliation of grouped transactions.
Sample Values: BULK_123456
Related Business Terms: Bulk Processing, Transaction Management, Batch ID, Reconciliation

# Column: cutoff_at
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: INTEGER
Description: The UNIX timestamp representing the exact moment a financial period ends, used to delineate the cutoff point for financial reporting or data aggregation.
Sample Values: 1614643200
Related Business Terms: UNIX Timestamp, Cutoff Time, Financial Reporting Period, Data Aggregation Deadline

# Column: payment_type
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: Specifies the method through which a payment was made. This can include various forms such as electronic transfers, cash payments, credit card payments, etc.
Sample Values: TRANSFER
Related Business Terms: Payment Processing, Transaction Method, Funds Transfer

# Column: payment_sub_type
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: Specifies the sub-category of the payment transaction, providing additional context beyond the primary payment type. This field is particularly useful for distinguishing between various kinds of transactions that fall under the same main category, such as differentiating between types of external payments.
Sample Values: EXTERNAL
Related Business Terms: Payment Processing, Transaction Classification, External Payments

# Column: created_at
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: INTEGER
Description: The UNIX timestamp representing the date and time when the record was created. This value is measured in seconds since the Unix Epoch (January 1 1970 00:00:00 GMT).
Sample Values: 1614556800
Related Business Terms: Unix Timestamp, Record Creation Time, Epoch Time

# Column: lifecycle_id
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: A unique identifier representing a specific lifecycle of a financial product or service. This ID tracks the entire lifecycle, from inception through to termination, of the product or service.
Sample Values: LIFECYCLE_20250301123456789
Related Business Terms: Lifecycle Management, Product Tracking, Service Lifecycle, Unique Identifier

# Column: payment_status
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: Indicates the current status of a payment transaction, reflecting whether it has been successfully completed, is pending, or has failed.
Sample Values: COMPLETED, PENDING, FAILED
Related Business Terms: {'term': 'COMPLETED', 'definition': 'The payment transaction has been successfully processed.'}, {'term': 'PENDING', 'definition': 'The payment transaction has been initiated but is not yet completed, often awaiting further action or confirmation.'}, {'term': 'FAILED', 'definition': 'The payment transaction could not be processed due to an error or rejection.'}

# Column: requested_execution_at
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: INTEGER
Description: The Unix timestamp representing the specific time at which the execution of a financial transaction was requested by the user. This timestamp is measured in seconds since the Unix Epoch (January 1, 1970).
Sample Values: 1614558000
Related Business Terms: Unix Timestamp, Execution Time, Transaction Request Time

# Column: sender_initiated_at
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: INTEGER
Description: The Unix timestamp representing the exact date and time when the sender initiated the transaction. This value is expressed as the number of seconds that have elapsed since 00:00:00 Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), Thursday, 1 January 1970, not counting leap seconds.
Sample Values: 1614557400
Related Business Terms: Unix Timestamp, Transaction Initiation Time, UTC

# Column: recurring_payment
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: BOOLEAN
Description: Indicates whether a payment is set to occur at regular intervals. A TRUE value means the payment is recurring, while a FALSE value indicates a one-time payment.
Sample Values: False
Related Business Terms: Subscription Model, Payment Schedule, Automatic Renewal

# Column: sender_transaction_amount
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: FLOAT
Description: This field represents the amount of money that the sender has transferred in a particular transaction. It is recorded in the transaction's currency and may include any applicable transaction fees.
Sample Values: 1000.5
Related Business Terms: Transaction Amount, Sender Amount, Transfer Amount

# Column: receiver_transaction_amount
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: FLOAT
Description: The total amount of money received in a transaction, expressed in the transaction's currency. This value represents the net amount credited to the receiver's account, excluding any fees or adjustments.
Sample Values: 1000.5
Related Business Terms: Transaction Amount, Net Received Amount, Transaction Value

# Column: number_of_payments
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: INTEGER
Description: This field represents the total number of payments scheduled for a financial transaction or obligation, such as a loan, lease, or any form of installment payment plan. It indicates the count of payments a borrower is obligated to make to fulfill the terms of the agreement.
Sample Values: 1
Related Business Terms: Installment Payments, Loan Repayment Schedule, Payment Plan, Amortization Schedule

# Column: sender_transaction_currency
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: The currency code representing the currency in which the transaction was initiated by the sender. This code follows the ISO 4217 currency code standard.
Sample Values: USD
Related Business Terms: ISO 4217, Transaction Currency, Sender Currency, Currency Code

# Column: sender_transaction_bank_account_number
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: This field represents the bank account number from which the transaction is initiated. It is unique to the account holder and is used to identify the sender's account in financial transactions.
Sample Values: ACCT12345678
Related Business Terms: Bank Account Number, Sender Account, Financial Transaction, Account Identification

# Column: sender_bank_name
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: The name of the bank from which the funds are sent. This field identifies the financial institution initiating the transaction.
Sample Values: First National Bank
Related Business Terms: Payment Processing, Bank Transfer, Financial Institution

# Column: sender_transaction_notes
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: This field contains notes or descriptions provided by the sender related to the purpose or details of the transaction. It is used to give context or additional information about the transaction to the recipient.
Sample Values: Payment for services
Related Business Terms: Transaction Details, Payment Description, Sender Notes

# Column: sender_bank_city
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: This field represents the city in which the sender's bank is located. It is used to identify the geographical location of the bank involved in the financial transaction.
Sample Values: New York
Related Business Terms: Bank Location, Transaction Origin, Geographical Identifier

# Column: sender_bank_postal_code
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: The postal code associated with the bank from which the funds are sent. This code helps in identifying the geographic location of the bank involved in the transaction.
Sample Values: 10001
Related Business Terms: Postal Code, Sender Bank, Geolocation, Banking Transaction

# Column: sender_bank_address
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: The physical address of the bank from which the funds are being sent. This includes details such as street name, number, city, and sometimes the postal code, depending on the country. It is crucial for legal and verification purposes during the transaction process.
Sample Values: 123 Wall Street
Related Business Terms: Bank Address, Sender Information, Transaction Details

# Column: sender_bank_country_code
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: The ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code representing the country of the bank initiating the transaction.
Sample Values: US
Related Business Terms: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, Banking, International Transactions, Country Code

# Column: receiver_bank_name
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: The name of the bank where the funds are being sent to in a financial transaction. This field captures the full legal name of the receiving financial institution.
Sample Values: Bank of America
Related Business Terms: Payment Processing, Bank Transfer, Financial Institution, Receiving Bank

# Column: receiver_bank_address
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: The physical address of the bank where the receiver's account is held, including street name, number, city, and postal code. This information is crucial for identifying the specific branch for transactions, especially in international wire transfers.
Sample Values: 555 Market Street
Related Business Terms: Bank Address, Receiver Information, Wire Transfer, Banking Details

# Column: receiver_bank_city
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: The city in which the receiver's bank is located. This information is crucial for processing domestic and international financial transactions, ensuring that funds are directed to the correct local or regional banking institution.
Sample Values: San Francisco
Related Business Terms: Bank Location, Transaction Processing, Funds Transfer, Banking Network

# Column: receiver_bank_bic
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: This field represents the Business Identifier Code (BIC) of the bank where the receiver's account is held. The BIC is an international code that uniquely identifies financial and non-financial institutions.
Sample Values: BOFAUS3N
Related Business Terms: BIC, SWIFT Code, International Bank Identifier, Receiver's Bank Identification

# Column: receiver_bank_country_code
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: This field represents the ISO country code of the bank where the recipient's account is held. It is used to identify the country in which the receiver's bank is located, facilitating international banking transactions.
Sample Values: US
Related Business Terms: ISO Country Code, International Banking, Bank Identification, Cross-border Transactions

# Column: session_id
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: A unique identifier for a user's session, typically used to track user activity or engagement within an application or website over a specific period.
Sample Values: SESS123456789
Related Business Terms: User Engagement, Session Tracking, User Activity Monitoring

# Column: receiver_bank_postal_code
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: The postal code associated with the physical location of the receiver's bank. This code is used to facilitate mail delivery and other services in the region where the bank is located.
Sample Values: 94105
Related Business Terms: Banking, Postal Code, Receiver Information, Financial Transactions

# Column: receiver_transaction_bank_account_number
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: This field represents the bank account number of the receiver involved in a transaction. It is a unique identifier used to route funds to the correct account during a financial transaction.
Sample Values: ACCT87654321
Related Business Terms: Bank Account Number, Financial Transaction, Funds Transfer, Receiver Identifier

# Column: receiver_city
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: The city in which the receiver of a transaction or shipment is located.
Sample Values: San Francisco
Related Business Terms: Shipping Destination, Transaction Location, Receiver Location

# Column: device_type
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: Indicates the type of device used to access the service or perform the transaction. This can include various categories such as mobile phones, tablets, desktop computers, and other electronic devices capable of accessing the internet or running applications.
Sample Values: MOBILE
Related Business Terms: User Engagement, Platform Usage, Device Analytics

# Column: device_longitude
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: FLOAT
Description: This field represents the longitudinal geographic coordinate where a device is located. Longitude values are measured in degrees, where negative values correspond to locations west of the Prime Meridian, and positive values correspond to locations east of the Prime Meridian.
Sample Values: -122.4194
Related Business Terms: Geolocation, Longitude, User Location, Device Tracking, Geospatial Analysis

# Column: receiver_transaction_currency
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: The currency in which the transaction amount is processed for the receiver. This field specifies the type of currency used in a financial transaction from the perspective of the recipient.
Sample Values: USD
Related Business Terms: Transaction Processing, Currency Code, Financial Transactions, International Transactions, Currency Conversion

# Column: receiver_country_code
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: This field represents the standardized two-letter country code of the country where the funds or services are being received. It adheres to the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 standard.
Sample Values: US
Related Business Terms: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, International Funds Transfer, Cross-border Transactions

# Column: device_ip_address
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: The unique numerical label assigned to each device participating in a computer network that uses the Internet Protocol for communication. This address serves both for identification and location addressing.
Sample Values: 192.168.1.1
Related Business Terms: IP Address, Network Security, Device Identification, Internet Protocol

# Column: device_latitude
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: FLOAT
Description: The geographical latitude coordinate where the device is located, expressed in decimal degrees. Positive values represent latitudes north of the equator, while negative values represent latitudes south of the equator.
Sample Values: 37.7749
Related Business Terms: Geolocation, Latitude, User Location, Device Positioning

# Column: event_external_id
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: A unique identifier assigned to events by external systems or partners. This identifier is used to reference the event across different platforms or databases outside the organization.
Sample Values: EXT12345
Related Business Terms: Event Management, External Integration, Unique Identifier

# Column: event_type
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: Specifies the type of financial event recorded in the transaction. This field categorizes the transaction by the nature of the financial activity it represents, such as payments, refunds, adjustments, etc.
Sample Values: PAYMENT
Related Business Terms: Transaction Processing, Financial Event, Payment Operations

# Column: info_type
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: Specifies the category of information being recorded, allowing users to distinguish between different types of data entries based on predefined categories.
Sample Values: INFO_TYPE_A
Related Business Terms: Data Classification, Record Type, Information Categorization

# Column: dispute_start_date
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: INTEGER
Description: The date on which a dispute was officially registered or initiated, represented as an integer in the format YYYYMMDD. This field is crucial for tracking the lifecycle of disputes and managing resolution timelines.
Sample Values: None
Related Business Terms: Dispute Resolution, Case Management, Compliance Tracking

# Column: dispute_reason
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: Describes the reason provided by a customer or a merchant for disputing a transaction. This field can include reasons such as fraudulent charges, services not provided, or incorrect transaction amount.
Sample Values: None
Related Business Terms: Chargeback, Dispute Management, Fraud Prevention, Customer Service

# Column: dispute_end_date
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: INTEGER
Description: The date on which a financial dispute was resolved or closed, represented as an integer in the format YYYYMMDD. A null value indicates that the dispute has not been resolved or the end date is not available.
Sample Values: None
Related Business Terms: Dispute Resolution, Financial Reconciliation, Account Settlement

# Column: dispute_notes
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: This field contains notes or comments related to disputes over transactions, charges, or other financial disagreements. It may include details on the nature of the dispute, actions taken, and the current status. This field can be particularly useful for financial analysts, customer service representatives, and compliance officers who are tracking the resolution of financial disputes.
Sample Values: None
Related Business Terms: Dispute Resolution, Transaction Dispute, Chargeback, Compliance, Customer Service

# Column: dispute_refunded
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: Indicates whether a transaction dispute was refunded. This field can be null if the refund status is not applicable or unknown.
Sample Values: None
Related Business Terms: Transaction Processing, Dispute Management, Refund Status

# Column: oob_start_date
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: INTEGER
Description: Represents the start date of an out-of-bounds (OOB) financial event or transaction, encoded as an integer. The value is typically formatted as YYYYMMDD. A null value indicates that the start date is not applicable or unknown.
Sample Values: None
Related Business Terms: Out-of-Bounds Transaction, Start Date, Financial Event

# Column: dispute_feedback_notes
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: This column contains textual notes or comments provided by the processing team or system regarding the feedback on disputes. These notes may include reasons for dispute decisions, additional information required, or any comments related to the dispute resolution process. The notes are intended for internal use to aid in the understanding and management of disputes.
Sample Values: None
Related Business Terms: Dispute Resolution, Feedback Comments, Processing Notes

# Column: dispute_submitted_by
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: Identifies the party who submitted the dispute. This could be the customer, merchant, or a third party acting on behalf of the customer.
Sample Values: None
Related Business Terms: {'term': 'Dispute', 'definition': 'A dispute occurs when a cardholder questions a transaction with their card issuer. The issuer creates a formal dispute, which immediately reverses the transaction.'}, {'term': 'Merchant', 'definition': 'A merchant is any type of business that sells goods or services.'}, {'term': 'Customer', 'definition': 'An individual or business that purchases goods or services from a merchant.'}, {'term': 'Third Party', 'definition': 'An entity that is involved in some way in an interaction that is primarily between two other entities, such as a merchant and customer. In the context of disputes, this could refer to a legal representative or a payment processor.'}

# Column: oob_comm_type
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: Specifies the type of out-of-band communication used in transactions or security protocols. This field identifies the method by which additional verification or communication is conducted outside of the primary transaction channel.
Sample Values: None
Related Business Terms: Out-of-Band Authentication, Two-Factor Authentication, Security Protocol, Transaction Verification

# Column: oob_end_date
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: INTEGER
Description: The date on which a business officially ceased operations, represented as an integer in the format YYYYMMDD. A null value indicates that the business is still operational or the end date is unknown.
Sample Values: None
Related Business Terms: Business Closure, End Date, Operational Status

# Column: oob_notes
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: This field captures any textual notes or comments related to out-of-balance situations within financial transactions or accounts. It is used for documenting reasons, adjustments, or any relevant information that explains why a transaction or account balance does not match expected values. This can include discrepancies found during reconciliation processes, errors identified, or any adjustments made to rectify the balance.
Sample Values: None
Related Business Terms: Reconciliation, Adjustments, Discrepancy, Out-of-Balance, Financial Transactions

# Column: oob_feedback_notes
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: This column captures any feedback notes provided through out-of-band (OOB) communication channels, such as emails, phone calls, or in-person meetings, regarding the performance, usability, or any other aspect of a product or service. These notes are valuable for qualitative analysis and for gaining insights that might not be captured through standard feedback mechanisms.
Sample Values: None
Related Business Terms: OOB Feedback, Qualitative Analysis, Customer Insights, Product Improvement

# Column: feedback_label
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: Categorizes user feedback into predefined labels for easier analysis and response. This field can be used to identify trends in user satisfaction and areas for improvement.
Sample Values: None
Related Business Terms: User Feedback, Customer Satisfaction, Product Improvement

# Column: sender_name
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: The name of the individual or entity initiating the transaction. This field captures the full name as a single string, including any middle names, initials, or suffixes.
Sample Values: John Doe
Related Business Terms: Transaction Originator, Payment Initiator, Sender Identity

# Column: feedback_type
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: Categorizes the nature of the feedback provided by a user or customer, indicating whether it is a complaint, suggestion, compliment, or inquiry. This field helps in analyzing customer feedback to improve products or services.
Sample Values: complaint, suggestion, compliment, inquiry
Related Business Terms: Customer Feedback Management, Quality Improvement, Customer Satisfaction, Service Enhancement

# Column: auth_method
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: Specifies the method used for user authentication within the system, indicating the security protocol for accessing accounts.
Sample Values: PASSWORD
Related Business Terms: Security Protocol, User Authentication, Access Control

# Column: sender_email
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: The email address of the individual or entity initiating the transaction or communication. This field captures the sender's email in a standardized format, facilitating contact tracing, authentication, and verification processes.
Sample Values: john.doe@example.com
Related Business Terms: Email Address, Sender Identification, Contact Information

# Column: sender_phone
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: This field represents the phone number of the individual or entity initiating the transaction. It is stored as a string of digits without any formatting, such as dashes or parentheses. The phone number includes the country code but excludes any leading zeros or plus signs.
Sample Values: 12125551234
Related Business Terms: Contact Information, Sender Details, Transaction Metadata

# Column: oob_response_type
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: Specifies the type of out-of-band (OOB) response used in a transaction or authentication process. This field can indicate the method through which a secondary verification is performed, such as SMS, email, or a push notification. A null value suggests that no out-of-band response was required or recorded.
Sample Values: None
Related Business Terms: OOB, Two-Factor Authentication, Multi-Factor Authentication, Security, Verification Process

# Column: sender_zip
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: The ZIP code from which the item was sent. This is used to identify the postal area of the sender's address.
Sample Values: 10001
Related Business Terms: Postal Code, ZIP Code, Sender Address Information

# Column: sender_dob
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: This field represents the date of birth of the individual or entity sending the transaction. The date is formatted as YYYY-MM-DD.
Sample Values: 1980-01-01
Related Business Terms: DOB, Sender Information, Personal Identification

# Column: sender_account_type
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: This field represents the type of account from which funds are being sent. It identifies whether the account is a checking, savings, or other types of financial account.
Sample Values: CHECKING
Related Business Terms: Payment Processing, Account Management, Fund Transfer

# Column: sender_account_currency
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: The currency code representing the currency of the funds in the sender's account. This code follows the ISO 4217 currency code standard.
Sample Values: USD
Related Business Terms: ISO 4217, Currency Code, Sender Account, International Transactions

# Column: sender_account_bic
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: The Business Identifier Code (BIC) of the account sending the transaction. It is an international code that uniquely identifies financial and non-financial institutions.
Sample Values: SNDRBANK123
Related Business Terms: BIC, SWIFT Code, Sender Identifier, Bank Identifier

# Column: receiver_id
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: A unique identifier assigned to entities receiving transactions or payments, ensuring accurate tracking and reporting of financial activities.
Sample Values: RCVR12345
Related Business Terms: Transaction Receiver, Payment Processing, Account Management

# Column: sender_account_balance
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: FLOAT
Description: This field represents the current balance of the sender's account in a financial transaction. It is a floating-point number that reflects the amount of money available in the account after the transaction has been initiated but before it has been completed.
Sample Values: 5000.75
Related Business Terms: Account Balance, Sender, Transaction Processing, Financial Operations

# Column: receiver_name
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: The full name of the individual or entity receiving the transaction or payment. This field captures the recipient's name as recorded in the transaction details, ensuring accurate identification for accounting and reporting purposes.
Sample Values: Jane Smith
Related Business Terms: Payee, Beneficiary, Recipient

# Column: receiver_phone
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: The phone number of the individual or entity receiving a transaction or communication. This number is expected to be in a standardized international format without spaces or special characters, starting with the country code.
Sample Values: 14155551234
Related Business Terms: Contact Information, Transaction Details, Communication

# Column: receiver_email
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: The email address of the individual or entity receiving the transaction or communication. This field is used to identify the recipient in various financial operations, such as payments, notifications, and account updates.
Sample Values: jane.smith@example.com
Related Business Terms: Recipient Identifier, Email Address, Transaction Receiver

# Column: receiver_street_addr
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: The street address of the recipient or receiver in a transaction. This address is used for billing or shipping purposes and includes the house number, street name, and any applicable suite or apartment numbers.
Sample Values: 555 Mission St
Related Business Terms: Billing Address, Shipping Address, Recipient Address

# Column: receiver_zip
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: The ZIP code associated with the address of the recipient in a transaction. This field captures the postal code where the receiver or beneficiary of a transaction is located, facilitating geographic analysis and validation of addresses.
Sample Values: 94105
Related Business Terms: Postal Code, Geographic Location, Address Validation

# Column: sender_occupation_status
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: Indicates the employment status of the sender at the time of the transaction. This field helps in understanding the sender's economic background and can be used for analytics related to financial behavior based on employment status.
Sample Values: EMPLOYED, UNEMPLOYED, SELF-EMPLOYED, RETIRED, STUDENT
Related Business Terms: {'term': 'Employed', 'definition': 'Indicates the sender is currently employed and receives a regular income.'}, {'term': 'Unemployed', 'definition': 'Indicates the sender is not currently employed and does not receive a regular income from employment.'}, {'term': 'Self-Employed', 'definition': 'Indicates the sender runs their own business or works on a freelance basis.'}, {'term': 'Retired', 'definition': 'Indicates the sender has retired from active employment and may receive a pension or retirement income.'}, {'term': 'Student', 'definition': 'Indicates the sender is currently enrolled in a full-time or part-time educational program and may not have a regular income.'}

# Column: receiver_dob
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: The date of birth of the individual or entity receiving the transaction or service. This field is used to verify identity and for age-related requirements.
Sample Values: 1985-05-15
Related Business Terms: DOB, Age Verification, Identity Verification

# Column: receiver_region
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: This field represents the geographical region or area code of the receiver in a transaction. It is used to identify the location within a country where the receiver of a transaction is based.
Sample Values: CA
Related Business Terms: Geolocation, Transaction Processing, Regional Analysis, Compliance Reporting

# Column: device_id
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: A unique identifier assigned to each device used in financial transactions. This ID helps in tracking and managing devices across various platforms and services.
Sample Values: DEV123456789
Related Business Terms: Device Management, Transaction Security, Asset Tracking

# Column: receiver_account_currency
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: This field specifies the currency in which the receiver's account is denominated. It is used to identify the currency type for transactions, ensuring that currency conversion and reconciliation processes can be accurately performed.
Sample Values: USD
Related Business Terms: Currency Code, Transaction Currency, Account Management

# Column: receiver_account_type
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: Indicates the type of account that is receiving funds in a transaction. This field specifies the nature of the receiver's bank account, such as whether it is a checking, savings, or other types of financial accounts.
Sample Values: CHECKING
Related Business Terms: Transaction Processing, Fund Transfer, Account Management

# Column: channel_type
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: This field represents the type of channel through which a transaction or interaction was initiated or completed. It categorizes the medium or platform used, providing insights into customer preferences and behavior.
Sample Values: MOBILE_APP
Related Business Terms: Customer Engagement Channels, Platform Type, Transaction Medium

# Column: sender_bank_branch_id
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: Unique identifier for the bank branch of the sender. This ID is used to specify the originating branch of a transaction or transfer.
Sample Values: BRANCH001
Related Business Terms: Bank Branch, Sender Identification, Transaction Origin

# Column: receiver_bank_sort_code
Table: test_data_event_store
Data Type: STRING
Description: A six-digit number that identifies the bank and branch where a bank account is held. Used primarily in the United Kingdom to route money transfers between banks.
Sample Values: 654321
Related Business Terms: Sort Code, Bank Identifier, Payment Routing

# Column: sender_bank_sort_code
